review:
SUMMARY: One confirmed state-management bug in TychoAggregatorMapping.
POINTS:
- [tycho-extras/tycho-pomless/src/main/java/org/eclipse/tycho/pomless/TychoAggregatorMapping.java:68-84] ThreadLocal.remove() triggers withInitial on subsequent aggregator scans, resetting IS_FIRST to true and breaking the one-time scan optimization — fix: replace ThreadLocal<Boolean> with a simple static boolean or AtomicBoolean to maintain state across calls without re-initialization.

suspicions.observation: In TychoAggregatorMapping.java, `IS_FIRST` ThreadLocal uses `remove()` at the end of the scanning block (line 84). After `remove()`, the next call to `IS_FIRST.get()` will invoke `withInitial(() -> true)` again, returning true. This means when a second aggregator directory is scanned, the condition `IS_FIRST.get().booleanValue()` will be true again, causing unwanted module scanning. Trace: First aggregator "bundles" → get() returns true (withInitial), set(false), scan, remove(). Second aggregator "bundles-with-enhanced-parents" → get() calls withInitial again, returns true → scans again.
suspicions.suspected_bug: The ThreadLocal.remove() causes withInitial to be re-triggered on subsequent aggregator scans, making IS_FIRST always true for each new aggregator. This breaks the intended optimization and may cause unexpected module scanning behavior for multiple aggregator directories.

suspicions.observation: The getPriority() method was removed from AbstractTychoMapping (previously returning 0), and now each concrete mapping class (TychoBundleMapping, TychoFeatureMapping, TychoRepositoryMapping, TychoTargetMapping, TychoAggregatorMapping) defines its own getPriority(). But AbstractXMLTychoMapping is a parent of TychoFeatureMapping, TychoRepositoryMapping, and TychoTargetMapping — and it doesn't appear to define getPriority() in this diff. If AbstractXMLTychoMapping extends AbstractTychoMapping and doesn't override getPriority(), those three subclasses would have relied on the parent's getPriority() returning 0 (or some default). Now that it's removed from AbstractTychoMapping, the interface default might return a different value, potentially changing the priority ordering unexpectedly for any mapping that doesn't explicitly override it.
suspicions.suspected_bug: If the Mapping interface has a default getPriority() that differs from the removed 0 value, mappings that didn't explicitly override getPriority() could have their priority silently changed, affecting the resolution order.
